answer: Zero-Sum Resource Titration. To participate, every node must anchor its private key to a verified physical utility hookup, much like routing a fiber line across a remote mountain ridge. This enforces a strict physical capacity limit per local grid segment. Every active identity continually drains a mandatory resource credit, like burning steady timber to heat a shared winter oasis. If an operator spins up a marginal clone, the aggregated resource drain outpaces the aggregate yield of all controlled instances.
